instruction: Add another layer to the image and label it 'Overlay'.

command: import time; import pyautogui; time.sleep(1); pyautogui.hotkey(['ctrl', 's']); time.sleep(1);

gimp -i -d -f -b '(let* ((image (car (gimp-file-load RUN-NONINTERACTIVE "/home/user/Desktop/white_background.xcf" "/home/user/Desktop/white_background.xcf"))) (layers (gimp-image-get-layers image)) (num-layers (car layers)) (layer-array (cadr layers)) (output-port (open-output-file "/tmp/gimp_layers.txt")) (i 0)) (while (< i num-layers) (let ((layer-name (car (gimp-item-get-name (aref layer-array i))))) (display layer-name output-port) (newline output-port)) (set! i (+ i 1))) (close-output-port output-port) (gimp-image-delete image) (gimp-quit 0))'
import time; import pyautogui; time.sleep(1); pyautogui.hotkey(['ctrl', 'q']); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new layer with name 'Overlay' in the GIMP XCF file. The evaluator uses a custom getter to extract layer names from the XCF file using GIMP's Script-Fu in batch mode, and a custom metric to check if the 'Overlay' layer exists in the layer list.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is semantically and logically correct for verifying the instruction.
Getter correctly uses GIMP Script-Fu in batch mode to extract layer names from the XCF file by loading the image, iterating through layers, and writing layer names to /tmp/gimp_layers.txt.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before extraction, ensuring the layer changes are persisted to the XCF file.
Metric correctly checks if 'Overlay' exists in the extracted layer names list using exact string matching, which is appropriate for layer name verification.
Data flow is correct: postconfig saves and extracts layer metadata -> getter reads the layer names from temp file -> metric validates 'Overlay' exists in the list.
Expected value 'Overlay' correctly matches the instruction requirement.
Parameter handling is correct: metric receives the rules dict directly as expected_state (per framework's get_rule behavior for type='rule') and correctly accesses expected_state.get('layer_name').
